1. Initial OSM building query and interactive Next.js / Leaflet map.
2. Expanded mapped building catalog to 11,659 polygons, STRtree index.
3. Earth Engine 2023 Google Open Buildings 2.5D estimated height enrichment; quality flags.
4. Approximate geometry-derived footprint areas and UI display.

10. Documentation generator and actual-file inventory.

## Maintenance rule
Update this milestone log **manually** when each capability is verified. The generator never claims to discover unrecorded past work. Add dates, verification logs, and known issues as development continues.

## Historical Flood GIS Integration — Step 8.99

### Source Dataset
- Dataset: Hyderabad Floods 2020 SpatialMap
- Original file: Flood_Affected_Areas_Mob_V3.kmz
- Source polygons: 13,321
- Pilot-intersecting polygon features: 9
- Repaired pilot polygon features: 1
- Preserved interior holes: 6

### Building-Level Spatial Analysis
- Building catalog: 11,659 OSM buildings
- Buildings overlapping historical mapped areas: 4,651
- Buildings without mapped overlap: 7,008
- Buildings with more than 90% mapped overlap: 4,550
- Total buildings with mapped overlap: 39.89%

### API Integration
- Building Intelligence API version: 0.6.0
- Historical overlap records loaded: 11,659
- Existing river and waterlogging proximity preserved
- Historical overlap evidence available for exact and nearby matches

### Frontend Integration
- Interactive Leaflet map
- Latitude/longitude search
- Predefined demo locations
- Government waterlogging markers
- Historical flood-area polygon overlay
- Historical overlap percentage and evidence panel
- Selected building polygon highlighting

### Verified Demo
- Building ID: osm-way-1193927888
- Historical mapped-area overlap: 100%
- Building footprint: approximately 222.59 m2
- Map overlay and building selection verified

### Limitations
- Historical flood-affected areas are not verified
  building-level inundation boundaries.
- Overlap does not establish water entry, flood depth,
  structural damage, or current flood risk.
- Source geometry and positional uncertainty remain.
- No validated flood-risk model has been developed.

### Next Research Objective
Compare October 2020 historical flood polygons with
Sentinel-1 VV/VH radar-change observations, using
appropriate spatial alignment and validation methods.


## Step 9.2 — Historical Polygon Category Validation

### Classification Results

The Hyderabad Floods 2020 SpatialMap dataset contains
nine polygon features intersecting the Moosarambagh pilot.

Seven features are named "Flood Affected Area" (SymbolID 0).
Two features represent named affected localities (SymbolID 3).

### Building Intersection Results

| Classification | Buildings |
|---|---:|
| No overlap | 7,008 |
| Generic flood-affected area only | 0 |
| Named locality only | 4,647 |
| Both categories | 4 |
| Total unique overlaps | 4,651 |

### Critical Finding

Only four buildings overlap polygons explicitly named
"Flood Affected Area".

All 4,651 buildings with combined historical polygon
overlap also intersect named-locality polygons.

Consequently, the previously calculated 39.89% figure
represents combined mapped-area coverage, not confirmed
historical building inundation.

### Methodological Limitations

- Source SymbolID meanings have not been independently verified.
- Named locality polygons are not established inundation boundaries.
- Generic flood-affected-area polygons also lack independent
  building-level inundation verification.
- Polygon positional accuracy has not been independently assessed.
- Source polygons may share underlying satellite observations
  with the AI NETRA Sentinel-1 experiment.

### Required Changes

1. Separate historical polygon categories in data processing.
2. Recalculate building-level overlap by category.
3. Update API evidence classifications.
4. Update frontend labels and map-layer presentation.
5. Avoid treating historical mapped-area overlap as flood ground truth.

### Evidence Status

Historical geographic affected-area evidence.
Building-level inundation remains unverified.


## Step 9.10.11 — Sentinel-1 Spatial Radar Validation

### Experiment
- Satellite: Sentinel-1A
- Collection: COPERNICUS/S1_GRD
- Orbit: Descending, relative orbit 165
- Polarizations: VV and VH
- Control period: 2020-09-27 to 2020-10-09
- Event period: 2020-10-09 to 2020-10-21
- Speckle filtering: 30 m focal median
- Analysis scale: 10 m
- Threshold: Backscatter change below -3 dB

### Validated Results

| Region | Area km2 | Samples | Control VV % | Event VV % | Control VH % | Event VH % |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Generic flood areas | 0.078863 | 969 | 2.10 | 40.28 | 3.97 | 72.25 |
| Named localities only | 2.652372 | 27104 | 13.33 | 1.38 | 5.67 | 2.22 |
| Outside both categories | 4.349056 | 43903 | 19.25 | 0.01 | 7.84 | 0.04 |

### Methodology
- Common valid-pixel mask across both periods and polarizations.
- Consistent raster sampling configuration.
- Identical sample counts within each region.
- Historical geographic categories analyzed separately.

### Interpretation
Generic flood-affected polygons exhibit substantially
greater negative radar-backscatter changes during the
event comparison than during the control comparison.

### Limitations
- Radar change does not independently establish flooding.
- Historical polygons are not verified inundation boundaries.
- Raster samples are spatially dependent.
- Reference polygon provenance remains uncertain.
- The event image was acquired after flooding began.
- No precision, recall, or flood-detection accuracy is claimed.

### Next Objective
Investigate whether Sentinel-1 radar-change evidence
can be associated with individual building footprints,
with explicit spatial-resolution and uncertainty limits.
